questions.q: What is the primary purpose of an Individualized Education Program (IEP)?
c: To tailor a free and appropriate public education to students with disabilities
To track the physical fitness of all students
To provide supports only within the PE classroom
To offer support to students with temporary injuries
questions.e: The Force demands balance. An IEP ensures each learner receives what they need through a Free Appropriate Public Education. This is not optional. It is law, structure, and purpose.

questions.q: During a PE class, a student receives specialized instruction, measurable goals, and formal supports documented in a legal plan. This is a:
questions.e: You must recognize the signs of true structure. Specialized instruction and measurable goals define an IEP. Without them, the plan lacks power.

questions.q: A teacher provides diagrams, verbal explanation, written instructions, and practice time when teaching a soccer pass. This best represents:
questions.e: A wise teacher does not rely on a single path. Like mastering multiple forms, VARK ensures all learners can access the skill through different modes.

questions.q: According to the CAST framework, the purpose of Universal Design for Learning (UDL) is to:
c: Identify and teach to the average learner
Design learning environments that remove barriers for all learners
Create a separate curriculum for students with disabilities
questions.e: The Jedi do not train for the average. UDL removes barriers so all may succeed. Design with intention, and access will follow.

questions.q: The IDEA principle of Least Restrictive Environment (LRE) requires that:
c: Students be placed in separate facilities
Students with disabilities be educated with nondisabled peers to the maximum extent appropriate
Schools provide the most expensive technology
questions.e: Isolation is not strength. Students must learn beside their peers whenever possible. Inclusion builds power in the system.

questions.q: Which is an example of Multiple Means of Action & Expression in PE assessment?
c: Allowing exit slip, verbal explanation, or referee role
questions.e: There are many ways to demonstrate mastery. A wise teacher allows students to show understanding through different forms. This is how true ability is revealed.

questions.q: Which is High-Tech assistive technology in physical education?
questions.e: Advanced tools extend capability. High-tech assistive technology removes barriers with precision and power. Use it wisely.

questions.q: A student has accommodations like extended time and visual supports but does NOT receive specialized instruction. This student likely has a:
questions.e: Not all require full intervention. A 504 Plan grants access without specialized instruction. Know the distinction. It is critical.

questions.q: Which of the following best represents Multiple Means of Engagement in PE?
c: Giving all students the same drill repeatedly
Allowing students to choose between activities or roles
Writing directions on the board only
questions.e: Engagement fuels effort. When students have choice, they invest. Motivation is not forced, it is cultivated.

questions.q: A teacher modifies a basketball activity by lowering the hoop and using a larger ball so a student can successfully participate. This is an example of:
questions.e: Adaptation is strategy, not weakness. Modify the task, and you unlock access. This is how inclusion is executed with precision.

questions.q: Which situation BEST reflects the principle of Least Restrictive Environment (LRE)?
c: A student is always placed in a separate adapted PE class
A student is excused from PE entirely
A student only observes from the sidelines
A student participates in general PE with supports and modifications
questions.e: Do not remove a learner from the system unless absolutely necessary. Support them within it. That is the discipline of true inclusion.

questions.q: A teacher allows a student to demonstrate understanding of a game strategy by explaining it verbally instead of writing it. This reflects:
questions.e: Mastery is not limited to one form. When students express understanding in different ways, you see their true capability. That is how you assess with wisdom.
